title: Giant nonlinearity of kinetic inductance in superconducting hybrid strip
authors: D. Yu. Vodolazov, Yu. P. Korneeva, M. A. Dryazgov, S. S. Ustavschikov, N. V. Porokhov, N. N. Osipov, I. Yu. Pashenkin, A. A. Korneev, M. A. Tarkhov
abstract: We demonstrate giant nonlinearity of the kinetic inductance $L_k$ in a superconducting NbN/Al hybrid strip. In contrast to ordinary superconductors, where the maximum observed current-induced variation of $L_k$ does not exceed tens of percent, we observe a 50-fold change in $L_k$. Physically, this effect is connected with the proximity-induced superconductivity in the Al layer and the specific choice of parameters for which the dependence of the superconducting current $I$ on the Cooper pair momentum $\hbar q$ exhibits a plateau at a current $I^*$ {\it well below} the depairing current. Formally, this leads to $L_k \sim dq/dI \to \infty$ as $I \to I^*$. We believe that our results open a new route for creating the next generation of highly sensitive detectors of electromagnetic radiation, calorimeters, parametric amplifiers, and magnetometers.
summary: This work demonstrates a giant, 50-fold nonlinearity in the kinetic inductance of superconducting $	ext{NbN/Al}$ hybrid strips. This effect arises from a plateau in the current-momentum relationship at a current well below the depairing limit. The findings suggest new pathways for developing highly sensitive quantum detectors, magnetometers, and parametric amplifiers.
main_problem: The paper investigates the phenomenon of 'giant nonlinearity' in the kinetic inductance ($L_k$) of superconducting hybrid strips.
main_result: The authors observed a 50-fold change in $L_k$, significantly exceeding the variation seen in ordinary superconductors. This nonlinearity is linked to a plateau in the current-momentum dependence of the superconducting current $I(q)$ at a current $I^*$ below the depairing current.
method: Measurements were performed using low-frequency impedance and two-coil techniques on $	ext{NbN/Al}$ hybrid strips to determine $L_k(I)$ and $L_k(T)$.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting $	ext{NbN/Al}$ hybrid strip. The theoretical understanding relies on analyzing the proximity-induced superconductivity in the Al layer, which dictates the relationship between superconducting current $I$ and Cooper pair momentum $\hbar q$.
key_observables: Kinetic inductance ($L_k$), current-induced variation of $L_k$, and the current-momentum dependence $I(q)$.
important_parameters: The nonlinearity is maximal near a characteristic current $I^*$ which is below the depairing current, and the effect is observed at temperatures around $T^* \approx 3 	ext{ K}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the physical effect is governed by the plateau in $I(q)$ leading to $L_k \sim dq/dI 	o \infty$ as $I 	o I^*$. Discrepancies with theory are attributed to edge defects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the measured $L(I)$ and calculated $I(q)$ dependence, showing the sharp nonlinearity. Other figures compare $L_k(T)$ measurements to theoretical predictions from the Usadel model.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental measurement of $L_k(I)$ and $L_k(T)$ in the hybrid strips, relates these measurements to the theoretical framework involving the Usadel equation, and concludes by discussing the implications of the observed giant nonlinearity for various quantum devices.
why_interesting: The strong, controllable nonlinearity in a superconducting parameter like $L_k$ offers a novel mechanism for building highly sensitive quantum sensors or non-linear elements, which is relevant to quantum measurement and circuit QED.
